claude.result:
Season 6 review complete. Key finding from checking all 5 prior seasons (not just the 2 the old notes covered): DAY_1_5/OVERNIGHT dominate every season and HD/TWILIGHT/FULL_DAY are always dead, but the "wait for autumn" calendar assumption is only partly right — season 5's breakout peaked in late May (doy150), not September/October, which a rigid calendar rule would have completely missed.

**What I changed:** Discovered the previous "hold-then-fire" strategy.py described in notes.md was never actually saved (the live file was still the do-nothing stub) — S02's budget leak to speculative THREE_QUARTER bets was pure manual-decision drift, not a strategy bug. I wrote and saved a real `strategy.py` that mechanically bans HD_AM/PM/TWILIGHT/FULL_DAY/THREE_QUARTER, fires only on a data-driven trailing-signal trigger (≥0.5 yt/angler over ≥4 boat-trips in the last 14 days) for DAY_1_5/OVERNIGHT, and books zero-PTO weekend slots only — no calendar anchor, so it can't miss an early breakout like season 5's.

**Why:** This directly targets the proven failure mode (manual discretion overriding a good thesis) rather than re-writing the thesis, and the reactive trigger fixes the calendar-rigidity blind spot the 5-season data exposed. Notes.md now instructs the nightly self to defer to the code and stop manual pre-signal spending.
